title: Geo-aware role safehouse and evidence archiver
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a geo-aware enforcement layer ("role safehouse") that constrains session bindings and role activation based on data residency and tenant jurisdiction, and build an evidence archiver that records compact, queryable audit bundles for periodic reviews and auditors. The feature aims to ensure that roles which grant access to data stored in specific jurisdictions cannot be activated from disallowed regions, and that all activation, delegation, and deprovisioning events are captured in a tamper-resistant archive with configurable retention and export policies. This solves gaps in our current access evidence pipeline where session provenance and jurisdictional constraints are not consistently correlated with SCIM/SAML events.
acceptance_criteria: A geo-policy engine evaluates each session token or SSO assertion at creation and denies role activation if the session's effective geo/location is outside the role's allowed jurisdictions.

Role activation and delegation events are emitted as structured audit records to the evidence archiver with a compact schema (actor, role, tenant, resource-scope, geo, timestamp, session-id, assertion-id).
Evidence archiver stores bundles encrypted-at-rest with tenant-scoped keys and supports retention TTL per-tenant or per-jurisdiction, configurable via the Console.
Exports: auditors can request signed export bundles (ZIP + signature) filtered by tenant, date-range, role, and jurisdiction. Exports include a manifest for verification.
Integration tests exercising SAML assertion replays, SCIM deprovision events, and manual session revocation demonstrate preserved ordering and evidence consistency.
Performance impact: median token evaluation latency added by geo-policy < 4ms on p99 path and feature toggled per-tenant.
technical_notes: We will implement the geo-policy engine as a lightweight evaluation step in the auth proxy (runtime sidecar), using a cached tenant policy store backed by a protobuf policy document.

Session location resolution: primary source SAML 'geolocation' claim if present, fallback to IP->geo lookup with cached max-age 5m. We will record both asserted and inferred geo to the evidence bundle.

Evidence archiver will batch incoming audit events into per-tenant daily bundles, sign with HSM-backed key material (via KMS integration), and persist to the tenant's residency zone (S3/gcs bucket with residency controls).
Retention enforcement: scheduled sweeper job will prune bundles based on tenant retention settings; deletions will emit deletion-proof markers included in exported manifests for auditors.
Schema: produce a minimal JSONL schema for events to keep bundle sizes small; use versioned schema and include change log metadata in each bundle.
Access controls: Console UI will call a new export API that requires role 'compliance.export' and uses approval flows for >30 day exports.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary tenants): enable geo-policy evaluation as 'audit-only' to collect false-positive telemetry and measure inferred geo accuracy.
Phase 2 (Opt-in enforcement): enable enforcement for tenants who have residency constraints and have completed policy review in Console.
Phase 3 (Default enforcement): after 4 weeks of opt-in stability, flip enforcement default for new tenants and provide migration tooling for existing tenants.
Migration tooling: provide a bulk-scan job that annotates existing active sessions and historical evidence with inferred geo and flags mismatches for admin review.
monitoring: SLOs: evidence_archiver_success_rate >= 99.9% over 7d; export_request_p95 < 2s for manifest generation
Dashboards: per-tenant geo mismatch heatmap; new alert when denials spike >10x baseline for a tenant (possible configuration/misrouting).
risks: IP->geo inference can be inaccurate for VPNs or corporate NATs; reliance on inferred geo risks false denies. Mitigation: keep audit-only phase and require explicit override workflow for verified exceptions.
Retention/deletion semantics may conflict with regulatory holds; we must surface legal hold overrides at the archiver level.
Large tenants may produce huge evidence bundles; we must ensure archiver scales and supports chunked exports and streaming downloads.
